goal: Reuse the loaded resident across HCLI rounds, worth a measured 6.2x on a 23-round ladder.
ATTEMPT: Memoise ResidentProcess by (binary, artifact_root, resident_binary, fusion_env, runtime_env) so successive engines share the child.
RESULT: FAILED. Two ResidentProcess.start calls, zero live shared children, call2/call1 = 0.973 -- 4.0 s saved out of a possible 211.
WHY_IT_FAILED: Caching the wrong layer. The object was reused; its CHILD had already been killed. hcli/runtime.py registers _atexit_stop() which calls pool.stop(), and the pool stops the backend (backends.py:2475 NoeticNativeBackend.stop), which calls connector.stop(), which calls resident.stop(). Every cli_main tears the resident down on the way out, so on the next call ResidentProcess.start() finds _alive() False and spawns again -- its reuse guard is correct and simply never gets the chance to fire.
THE_FIX_IS_LOCATED_PRECISELY: Not construction, TEARDOWN. A persistent-resident mode needs the pool to leave the child running (or to attach to an externally supervised one) rather than stopping it at exit. That is a lifetime change in hcli/runtime.py, not a caching trick in a sidecar.
A_BUG_I_MADE_AND_FIXED_ON_THE_WAY: The first version of the patch wrote obj.__hawking_fresh inside the class body, which mangles to _Shared__hawking_fresh, and read it back with getattr(self, '__hawking_fresh'), which does NOT mangle. The flag was written under one name and read under another, so __init__ never ran and _alive() hit a missing attribute. Fixed by using a single-underscore name.
HONEST_STATUS: The 6.2x remains available and is NOT yet realised. What this attempt bought is the exact location of the blocker, which the projection alone did not give.
PRE_COMMITTED_KILL_FOR_THE_REAL_FIX: If the pool is made to leave the resident running and a second cli_main still shows a complete_payload above 60 s, the load is not what persists and the lifetime change is the wrong fix.
